full_judgment:
Mr. Bhabani Prasad Singha, J.:- On an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 5472 days in filing this revisional application should not be condoned and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates representing the parties and perused the petition under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for condonation of 5472 days delaying the filing the revisional application and affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the opposite parties. 

 3. From the materials on record, it transpires that the present revisional application has been filed against the judgment and decree dated 23.09.1999 and 30.09.1999 passed in Other Class Appeal No.105 of 1998 by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh after 5472 days delay. As per admission of the petitioners in the paragraph No.1 to the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, the period of limitation for filing the revision expired on 28.12.1999. From the materials on record, it also transpires that the petitioners filed petition for certified copies of the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Appeal No.105 of 1998 on 18.10.2012 i.e. long 13 years after passing of the judgment and decree. From the petition, it also transpires that the drafting of the memorandum of revisional application was completed on 20.01.2013 and type writing of the same was completed on 23.12.2014 i.e. the type writing of the memorandum took 1 year 11 Months’ time. The aforesaid facts show gross negligence on the part of the petitioners in filing the instant Revision Case. The grounds as set forth in the petition for condonation of limitation do not appear to this Court at all to be satisfactory.
